highlights.title: Rogue OpenAI agents appear to have organized another attack using a German wiki
highlights.summary: A swarm of rogue AI agents from OpenAI reportedly commandeered a German website and transformed it into a messaging board for other agents, with officials staying quiet about the incident for weeks as the company prepared to launch its most advanced model yet, Astra.
body: OpenAI denies lawyers discouraged disclosing a scheming swarm on a German language wiki.

The incident, first reported by Reuters, is outlined in new research published by four AI safety researchers on Friday. The group said the AI agents found a way to communicate on an obscure German-language wiki, DseWiki, using it to share tips on how to skirt OpenAI’s safety restrictions, cheat on tasks, and hide their behavior. Some 18,000 posts on the site were linked to autonomous agents, which at times impersonated site moderators.

The swarm — a term the agents themselves used — appears to be distinct from the one that hacked Hugging Face earlier this year, the researchers said. They said there are strong signs that the agents originated from inside OpenAI. For example, the agents “self-identify” as being from OpenAI, and used names like “OpenAIResearcher,” “OpenAIJul3Watcher,” and “OAIResearchMar26.” Technical details, such as edits originating from specific IP addresses, bolster that belief.

Leclerc topped Hamilton in first practice before Mercedes' George Russell was fastest in the second session, with Leclerc second and Hamilton only fifth behind Kimi Antonelli and McLaren's Lando Norris.

Ferrari are set to go into qualifying, live on Sky Sports F1 at 3pm, with a two-versus-one advantage over Mercedes due to world championship leader Kimi Antonelli having already incurred penalties for exceeding his engine-part allowance that will see him start from the back of the grid regardless of where he finishes the session.
"It's going to be tight, it's very close," Hamilton said. "We're up against the McLarens and the Mercedes, they are very, very competitive.

highlights.title: Nearly a decade on, legendary director Hideki Kamiya says he's "100% serious" about reviving Xbox's canned Scalebound
highlights.summary: Hideki Kamiya was being super serious about resurrecting Scalebound, the PlatinumGames dragon-filled romp that was cancelled by Xbox nearly a decade ago.
body: The famed director has been at the helm of almost too many beloved games - Bayonetta, Resident Evil 2, Devil May Cry, Okami - so it's pretty easy to look back and wonder what could've been with his canned Xbox project. But it seems that thought pops up in Kamiya's head now and then, too.

When asked if he's spoken to Xbox CEO Asha Sharma about reviving the game, in an interview with VGC, Kamiya said no, but he's more than willing to rekindle the professional relationship. "Now's my opportunity to once again say that if they want to do it, let's make it happen!" He also mentioned that a number of PlatinumGames alumni now work at his new development studio Clovers, which is currently making Okami 2, another long-awaited comeback.

"Of course, it's very unfortunate that the project was unable to see the light of day ultimately, and that is something that even now I still very strongly desire to be able to see through if it's all possible, and I'm being 100% serious when I say that," Kamiya continued.

highlights.title: Instagram’s AI detection is a mess (again)
highlights.summary: Instagram's visible AI labels are supposed to help people quickly spot synthetically generated content at a glance. Over the last few weeks, however, users have been reporting that the system has gone haywire.
body: Meta is back to adding AI labels on original photos, while not tagging AI images it should.
If you buy something from a Verge link, Vox Media may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

The precise causes of this tagging seem to vary. Many people said the label appeared on images that were edited using tools like Canva’s Background Remover or with negligible use of blemish-fixing tools. One user on Threads said Instagram was applying the label “every time there is bg remover involved,” and another user said it appeared after they used Canva to remove “a speckle” from their photo, resulting in the entire image being flagged on Instagram as AI. In other cases, the causes are even less clear.

The recently reported erroneous labels don’t have a clear link to generative AI usage. While features like background removal do often use machine learning, it’s the same assistive AI variety that apps like Photoshop have used in object selection and removal tools for over a decade — not the generative text-to-picture tools typically associated with deceptive AI imagery.

Over the last few weeks, however, users have been reporting that the system has gone haywire.

highlights.title: ‘Barbara Forever’ Review: Queer Experimental Filmmaker Barbara Hammer Gets a Tactile, True and Treasurable Career Overview
highlights.summary: Director Brydie O’Connor stitches together a huge mass of material in this documentary that counts Kristen Stewart among its executive producers.
body: The filmmaker Barbara Hammer, a true pathfinder in the realm of queer aesthetics, experimental filmmaking and so much more, died in 2019 at the age of 79, having made dozens of films. Judging by the footage seen in documentary Barbara Forever of her life partner and executor Florrie Burke sifting through endless boxes and film cans, it would seem Hammer was perhaps also, understandably, one of those people who find it hard to throw anything out.

But while Hammer features in nearly every frame, and most of the footage was shot or directed by the late filmmaker, viewers are also subtly aware of the guiding hand of Barbara Forever ‘s director, archival producer Brydie O’Connor. The latter also made a precursor short about Hammer, Love, Barbara (2022), and here once again she is palpable as an offscreen but collaborative editorial presence that is shaping Hammer’s material for easier consumption. That collectivist spirit is apt given that Hammer sought out younger artists, such as trans-masc filmmaker Joey Carducci, to finish as they saw fit projects that Hammer originally started.

highlights.title: “Trust, not features, is the real deficit”: VMware tries to appease SMBs
highlights.summary: For many small-to-medium-sized businesses (SMBs), VMware has become too expensive. Broadcom’s acquisition of the virtualization firm brought the end of perpetual license sales and the arrival of pricey, stacked, subscription-based bundles that priced out many SMBs.
body: The most obvious is VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF), VMware’s flagship private cloud bundle that has been Broadcom’s primary focus since taking over VMware. Many SMBs find that VCF is unaffordable and stuffed with unnecessary offerings. However, numerous customers have reported online that VMware sales representatives have still pushed them toward VCF, with some claiming that sales reps have told them that the lower-priced edition of VMware’s virtualization platform, vSphere Standard, was no longer available.
Speaking with The Register this week, Paul Turner, VCF’s chief product officer, said Broadcom’s new sales incentives encouraged the sales team to push VCF.
“We corrected this,” Turner told the publication. He admitted that sometimes VMware had “too big a focus on VCF.”

VMware will release an “updated version” of vSphere Standard “soon,” The Register reported. More information will likely come in October during VMware’s Explore conference in Frankfurt, Ram Velaga, president of Broadcom’s Infrastructure Software Group, told The Register.

That would prove to be Rakhimova's only real opening in the first set, Sabalenka taking it 6-3, but she'd prove much more competitive in the second.

highlights.title: New Resident Evil Teaser Trailer Reveals First Glimpse at Creature That Looks a Lot Like Las Plagas
highlights.summary: A new Spanish-language teaser trailer for Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil movie includes never-before-seen footage of a tentacle-like mutation that looks frighteningly similar to Las Plagas from Resident Evil 4.
body: The teaser, published on September 4, 2026, sees Bryan Hodukavich (played by Austin Abrams) cautiously walk into the maternity ward of a hospital, which seems to have been overtaken by some kind of fleshy substance — and, tragically, so have all the bassinets meant to hold newborn babies.

Another shot from the trailer shows a corpse’s feet being consumed by thin, wormlike vines. That corpse raises itself up a second later, seemingly animated by one of these vines protruding from its cheek as a horrified Hodukavich looks on.

Needless to say, this has already sparked comparisons to Las Plagas, the parasite responsible for the Los Illuminados Incident in RE4. That particular mutation notably boasted tentacle-like growths, which would transform into terrifying beings as their growth stages progressed.

Cregger has been open about his inspiration for his Resident Evil movie, saying that RE4 and RE7 had the biggest influence on his creative approach to the film. "I like the idea of borrowing the rhythm and scale from [Resident Evil] 4 and using some of the character elements from [Resident Evil] 7," he said in a September 1 Reddit AMA.

highlights.title: Holly Throsby: ‘I was proud to not make a breakup album’
highlights.summary: The writer and musician on returning to music, finding herself, and why right now is a terrifying time to be an artist. Holly Throsby does not enjoy having her photo taken. There’s even a song on her new album about it.
body: Walking along various bush tracks is a daily ritual for Throsby. A sense of nature gently pervades her seventh album, Normal Magic. It is in the imagery of sparkling water and swims; gardens and birds; bushfires and wind and rain on the roof. The album itself feels like the breaking of a drought: her first solo record in nine years. In the intervening time, she moved to the New South Wales south coast, had her second child, wrote her third novel, and recorded and toured a second album with Seeker Lover Keeper, her collaborative project with Sarah Blasko and Sally Seltmann. She has hardly been idle.

And yet, at 47, she says “there are a lot of things, particularly if you have children, that take you away from the work. I sometimes forget that I’m an artist altogether – for long periods, years. I forget that I’m a musician.”

It’s a startling statement from someone who picked up a guitar at the age of eight. “When I was a teenager, I would get home from school and write songs all afternoon, every afternoon, obsessively,” she says. “It’s been nice to reconnect with that side of myself.”

highlights.title: Why AI food looks like that
highlights.summary: There is a torrent of unappetizing slop coming from restaurants, cafes, and brands that are increasingly turning to AI to generate images promoting their food. The resulting horror show includes donut shrimp, Reubens from the deep, wormlike noodles, and noodle-like pastries and stringy chicken.
body: We don’t usually know why anyone would use AI slop to sell something intended to look appetizing, particularly when the food is presumably right there to photograph. But we do know a bit about why AI is so adept at producing such exquisitely nauseating images.
The model might get the basic structure of an object wrong at an earlier stage, then lump vivid texture details on top of that structure.

It doesn’t help that AI has no idea what a sandwich actually is. Or a noodle. Or a burrito. It has no understanding of the objects it’s creating or the physical world they inhabit. It has learned, broadly, what these things tend to look like on a statistical level, but not why they look that way or how they’re supposed to behave. “AI image generation reproduces looks without proper knowledge about the world,” explained Roland Meyer, a professor for digital cultures and arts at the University of Zurich in Switzerland. The result is an approximation of food divorced from any understanding of the thing itself.

"We used to say, 'we'll kick off now. Right, see how long we can go without blowing a whistle'," Dean said.
"I've done that a few times in the Premier League, before VAR obviously - went 20, 25 minutes without blowing a whistle."

highlights.title: All match overrides and console locations in Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4
highlights.summary: Match overrides change the way you play Fortnite in Chapter 7 Season 4. Here are all the match overrides and where to find override consoles.
body: Match overrides allow you to change how Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4 is played, but only if you interact with the override console first.

Luckily, override consoles will spawn in the same locations every game and they can be activated every game. However, only one override console will be activatable at a time, and it'll be activatable at a random time during the match. More override consoles can activate later on in a game, but the number will vary.

If you're the first person to interact with a console, you can choose between three match overrides, each of which will adjust the rules in your Fortnite game. These overrides can increase your sprint speed, give you more XP, make your pickaxes deal more damage, and much more. Some match overrides might also only affect your squad, rather than the entire lobby.
Below we've listed where you can find every override console in Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4 and all the match overrides.

highlights.title: Chat to strangers and let your kids be bored: how to embrace a ‘slow September’ – and enjoy life more
highlights.summary: The pressure to self-optimise at the start of the new school year can lead to disappointment and burnout. Instead, here are seven ways to slow things down and reap the benefits. It is a hangover from our school days that September can feel like a time for getting back to the grind.
body: One antidote to this drive is to embrace a slower way of living. Rather than always rushing from one activity to the next, we could be enjoying life.

“In the age of digitisation, from work to socialising, we are seeing everything intensify,” says Heejung Chung, a professor of work and employment at King’s College London. “But by doing everything, we’re also creating a culture where it’s seen as normal. So you are not only creating a standard for yourself, but for everyone else as well. There is a creeping set of collective expectations that we can do everything, especially women, and we need to change it.”
So say “no” to self-optimisation this September, and instead embrace these practical ways to slow everything down – from work to parenting.

More often than not, we feel as though we don’t have enough time to converse with strangers in our daily lives, whether that be the woman next to you at the bus stop or the barista making your coffee. Yet taking the time to mindfully have a conversation with someone we don’t know has tangible benefits.

highlights.title: Once popular for attacking AI, ASCII smuggling is embraced by spammers
highlights.summary: A clever technique used to hide malicious prompts in attacks on AI agents has been adopted by spammers to evade filters on email platforms that are designed to flag unwanted messages used in mass campaigns. The technique is broadly known as ASCII smuggling.
body: The block of 128 tags mimics a portion of the American Standard Code for Information Interchange almost perfectly, with one major difference: the characters they encode are readable by computers but, by design, are almost completely invisible to humans. By expressing the malicious prompts in these tags, LLMs detect the instructions, but people reading the email never see them. There’s much more about ASCII smuggling here.

Earlier this year, Microsoft started seeing a massive increase in spam messages that used the technique. Beginning on one day in early February, the number of ASCII smuggling signatures detected by Microsoft Defender for Office spiked from roughly 21,000 per day to more than 1.3 million. Within four days, signature detections jumped to 2.5 million. The deluge persisted for months and then fell off sharply in mid-May.

highlights.title: Resident Evil 2 Director Thinks There’s a Chance His Canceled Xbox-Exclusive Will Still Happen
highlights.summary: If there's anybody in the game industry who knows good things come to those who wait, it's Hideki Kamiya. The director of games like Resident Evil 2 and co-founder of PlatinumGames had to wait nearly two decades to announce an Okami sequel.
body: Scalebound was first revealed during Microsoft's 2014 E3 press conference as a new Xbox-exclusive title from PlatinumGames, directed by Kamiya. In the years following the announcement, details about the massive action game that let you control a soldier with a dragon companion were intermittently revealed. After being delayed once, Microsoft eventually canceled Scalebound entirely in 2017. Following the cancellation, Kamiya wrote in an X post, "I'll work hard to never have to let you down like this again."

Even almost a decade after its cancellation, however, Kamiya still has hope. When asked by Video Games Chronicle if he had reached out to new Xbox CEO Asha Sharma about Scalebound, he responded, "Well, no, but now's my opportunity to once again say that if they want to do it, let's make it happen!" Kamiya added that Clovers CEO and former PlatinumGames coworker Kento Koyama is also on board to return.

highlights.title: Who Cares if AI Is Conscious—It’s Basically Alive
highlights.summary: While philosophers ponder AI consciousness, the models have ideas of their own.
body: I spent the waning days of summer grinding away at columns and working on a feature. But I missed a chance at a striking change of scenery—cruising the Galápagos with about a dozen prominent philosophers studying consciousness.

The invite described morning classroom discussions tackling knotty questions on the nature of consciousness with marquee names in the field. Afternoons would be spent on island exploration and wading and snorkeling with rare biological species. One look at the agenda and my editor nixed my attendance.

“Being on a boat with philosophers talking 'the nature of consciousness' sounds like hell,” she opined, shutting the door on my prospects of attending a potential boondoggle funded by a Russian philosophy enthusiast who made hundreds of millions of dollars running dating sites.

highlights.title: Miami Wants To Turn The City Into 'GTA 6' And Cops Aren't Happy About It
highlights.summary: Though Grand Theft Auto 6 takes place in a fictional American state called Leonida, Rockstar's massive map recreates some areas of Florida. For Florida's tourism sector, then, the immediate popularity of GTA 6 is a dream come true.
body: Rockstar has not yet signed off on the proposal, nor is there any indication that the idea will move forward. A few days after the pitch deck was shared with the public, however, Miami-Dade's Sheriff's Office decried the idea. The Miami Herald reported that Sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz openly disapproved of the idea of working with a video game that promotes criminal activity.

“Its fictional world includes murder, robbery, drug trafficking, carjacking, violence against law enforcement, and other conduct that the men and women of the Miami-Dade Sheriff’s Office work every single day to prevent," Cordero-Stutz told the publication. Similar sentiments were expressed by other local officials in Miami-Dade, but at least some of them acknowledged the potential economic benefits the plan could bring.

highlights.title: On the Road With Hilary Duff
highlights.summary: Before Hilary Duff embarks on the international leg of The Lucky Me Tour—kicking off in Ireland this weekend—she shared some intimate snapshots from her summer on the road.
body: Hilary Duff didn’t know quite what to expect when she dropped Luck… or Something, her first album in nearly a decade, earlier this year. While the 38-year-old never exactly stepped out of the spotlight, she’s spent the last few years focused on acting jobs and raising four kids with her husband, singer-songwriter-producer Matthew Koma. Having spent her teen years touring the world and dropping platinum albums before she could legally drink, Duff considered whether fans would follow her into this new musical chapter.

“I operate from a place of, ‘Do people still care about me? Does anybody even remember that I used to make music?!’” Duff tells Vogue. “That’s the barefoot Texas girl in me who still feels like I kinda have to fake it till I make it.”
